newsitem.title: UK: EUROPEAN FUNDS SELL SHARES, STOCKPILE CASH - SURVEY.
newsitem.headline: EUROPEAN FUNDS SELL SHARES, STOCKPILE CASH - SURVEY.

text.p: Continental European fund managers are selling local shares and parking the money in cash, a survey by Merrill Lynch said.

The survey, which covered 70 institutions managing $653 billion, found that sellers of Continental European equities outnumbered buyers by seven percent in August, the most bearish sentiment since the survey began in 1994.

"Managers are unkeen to invest in any equity market and are raising cash," Merrill Lynch said. "The number of managers looking to raise cash exceeds by 17 percent the number who are looking to invest cash."
Interest in Pacific Basin equities took a tumble, with buyers outnumbering sellers by one percent, down from 14 percent last month.
European fund managers are also net sellers of local bonds, with 14 percent more sellers than buyers.
The euro is expected to be a soft currency by 79 percent of respondents, with 93 percent expecting Spain to be in the first wave. Italy is expected by 59 percent to be in the first wave.
The survey was carried out for Merrill by Gallup between August 1 and 6. -- James Saft, London newsroom +44 171 542 2734
